title: RXO’s Latest Curve Freight Market Forecast Marks the Tenth Consecutive Quarter of Spot Rate Inflation
summary: While the Curve has declined sequentially in the fourth quarter to date, it is still significantly higher than 2025 heading into peak season.
body_markdown:
- *The Curve, RXO’s proprietary truckload spot rate index, climbed even higher in the third quarter, hitting its highest level since 2021.*
- *While* *the Curve has declined sequentially in the fourth quarter to date, it is still significantly higher than 2025 heading into peak season.*


**CHARLOTTE, N.C. – November 16, 2026** –[RXO](http://www.rxo.com/) (NYSE: RXO), a leading provider of asset-light transportation solutions, today released the latest update to its proprietary Curve truckload market forecast, which shows strong year-over-year spot rate growth, excluding the impacts of fuel.


In the third quarter, spot rates, as measured by the Curve, started off strong in July. Though rates moderated in August and September, the index still finished the quarter at 37.9%, its highest level since 2021 and an increase from 32.4% in the second quarter.


Through November 13th, the Curve is tracking lower on a sequential basis yet is still on pace to finish the fourth quarter well into inflationary territory.


Ongoing carrier capacity attrition, driven by federal regulation enforcement and rising carrier costs, has led to a supply imbalance relative to demand. This dynamic is sustaining the year-over-year increases in spot rates.


“The early weeks of the third quarter marked some of the most volatile capacity and spot rate conditions we’ve experienced in years,” said Corey Klujsza, vice president of pricing and procurement at RXO. “As we moved deeper into the summer, muted freight demand combined with increasing contract rates stabilized the spot market relative to the start of the quarter. That said, we’re still in a very different market than we were at this time last year, and any seasonal demand outperformance could reignite rate and capacity volatility.”


Jared Weisfeld, chief strategy officer at RXO, said, “Despite increasing imports, healthier inventory levels, and manufacturing growth, overall freight demand remains muted. Continued pressure on the supply side, including federal policy enforcement, record-high diesel prices, and an increased cost of capital, has supported the truckload market recovery. Higher truckload rates would typically bring capacity back into the market, but those same pressures are limiting driver reentry. The market remains highly susceptible to increases in demand.”


To read the full fourth-quarter Curve report, visit[https://rxo.com/resources/research/us-truckload-market-guide/](https://rxo.com/resources/research/us-truckload-market-guide/) .


The Curve exemplifies RXO’s commitment to providing market-based, data-driven insights that help shippers and carriers navigate the dynamic truckload market.
